<vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Simple Cholesky decomposition (sequential, unblocked algorithm)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            \n            if (i == j) {\n                // Diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[j * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                const double val = A[j * n + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    return false;\n                }\n                A[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            } else {\n                // Off-diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[i * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                A[i * n + j] = (A[i * n + j] - sum) / A[j * n + j];\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // Zero out upper triangular part\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n    \n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    \n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n    \n    // Compute A = B * B^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n    \n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n    \n    // Compute L * L^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n        \n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    \n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n    \n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n    \n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A; // Save original for validation\n    }\n    \n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n);\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n    \n    if (!success) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n    double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n    double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return 0;\n}\n","userModified":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01EsFy9K8ChmKnTu5oSwd1Lu","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

L overwrites the lower triangle and the upper triangle is zeroed.\n//\n// Each panel of NB columns is processed in three phases:\n//   1. factor the NB x NB diagonal block               (potrfDiagKernel, one thread block)\n//   2. solve for the rows of the panel below it        (trsmPanelKernel)\n//   3. update the trailing lower triangle              (gemmNTKernel<true>, tiled GEMM)\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                                  \\\n    do {                                                                                  \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);     // outputs computed per thread per dimension\nconstexpr int GEMM_TILE = GEMM_DIM * GEMM_MICRO; // 64 x 64 output tile\nconstexpr int GEMM_BK = 16;       // K-step staged in shared memory\n\n// Copy the lower triangle of the b x b diagonal block at (k0, k0) into shared memory.\n__device__ void loadLowerBlock(double (*S)[NB], const double* A, size_t n, int k0, int b) {\n    for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < b * b; idx += blockDim.x) {\n        const int r = idx / b, c = idx % b;\n        if (c <= r) S[r][c] = A[(size_t)(k0 + r) * n + (k0 + c)];\n    }\n}\n\n// Unblocked Cholesky of the diagonal block at (k0, k0), executed by a single thread block.\n// Records the smallest failing global diagonal index in *failIdx (INT_MAX if none).\n__global__ void potrfDiagKernel(double* A, size_t n, int k0, int b, int* failIdx) {\n    __shared__ double S[NB][NB];\n    loadLowerBlock(S, A, n, k0, b);\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int j = 0; j < b; ++j) {\n        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (int k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += S[j][k] * S[j][k];\n            }\n            const double val = S[j][j] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                atomicMin(failIdx, k0 + j);\n            }\n            S[j][j] = sqrt(val);\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        for (int i = j + 1 + threadIdx.x; tiles entirely above\n// the diagonal are skipped.\ntemplate <bool LOWER>\n__global__ void gemmNTKernel(double* C, size_t ldc, const double* X, const double* Y, size_t ld,\n                             int M, int N, int K, double alpha, double beta) {\n    if (LOWER && blockIdx.x > blockIdx.y) return;\n\n    __shared__ double As[GEMM_BK][GEMM_TILE + 1];\n    __shared__ double Bs[GEMM_BK][GEMM_TILE + 1];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x, ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const int tid = ty * GEMM_DIM + tx;\n    const int rowBase = blockIdx.y * GEMM_TILE;\n    const int colBase = blockIdx.x * GEMM_TILE;\n\n    double acc[GEMM_MICRO][GEMM_MICRO] = {};\n\n    for (int k0 = 0; Returns false if not positive definite.\nbool choleskyDecomposition(double* dA, const size_t n) {\n    if (n == 0) return true;\n\n    int* dFail = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dFail, sizeof(int)));\n    const int noFail = INT_MAX;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dFail, &noFail, sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    for (size_t k0 = 0; k0 < n; k0 += NB) {\n        const int b = (int)std::min<size_t>(NB, n - k0);\n        const size_t r0 = k0 + b; // first row below the diagonal block\n        const int rows = (int)(n - r0);\n\n        potrfDiagKernel<<<1, NB>>>(dA, n, (int)k0, b, dFail);\n\n        if (rows > 0) {\n            trsmPanelKernel<<<(rows + TRSM_THREADS - 1) / TRSM_THREADS, TRSM_THREADS>>>(\n                dA, n, (int)k0, b, r0);\n\n            // Trailing update: A22 -= P * P^T, where P = A[r0.., k0..k0+b)\n            double* C = dA + r0 * n + r0;\n            const double* P = dA + r0 * n + k0;\n            gemmNTKernel<true><<<dim3((rows + GEMM_TILE - 1) / GEMM_TILE,\n                                      (rows + GEMM_TILE - 1) / GEMM_TILE),\n                                 dim3(GEMM_DIM, GEMM_DIM)>>>(\n                C, n, P, P, n, rows, rows, b, -1.0, 1.0);\n        }\n    }\n\n    const size_t total = n * n;\n    zeroUpperKernel<<<(total + 255) / 256, 256>>>(dA, n);\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n    int fail = noFail;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(&fail, dFail, sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dFail));\n\n    if (fail != INT_MAX) {\n        printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", (size_t)fail);\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix directly in device memory\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(double* dA, const size_t n) {\n    if (n == 0) return;\n\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    double* dB = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dB, n * n * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dB, B.data(), n * n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    // Compute A = B * B^T\n    gemmNT(dA, n, dB, dB, n, (int)n, (int)n, (int)n, 1.0, 0.0);\n\n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    addDiagonalKernel<<<(n + 255) / 256, 256>>>(dA, n, (double)n);\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dB));\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const Only `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt` were changed; no files were added, and the executable name is still `cholesky`.\n\n**What changed**\n- **Factorization:** a blocked, right-looking algorithm with a 64-column panel. Each panel runs three kernels: a single-block diagonal factorization, a row-parallel triangular solve for the panel below, and a tiled GEMM for the trailing lower triangle. The upper triangle is zeroed on the device, as the original did.\n- **Matrix generation:** the random matrix `B` is still produced on the host with the same `rand_r` sequence, so the input values are unchanged. The `B·Bᵀ` product and diagonal shift now run on the GPU.\n- **Validation:** `L·Lᵀ` is computed on the GPU; the element-wise comparison stays on the host, using the same tolerance.\n- **CMake:** the project enables the CUDA language, compiles `cholesky.cpp` as CUDA, targets `native` architectures, and keeps the host optimization flags via `-Xcompiler`. No new dependencies: only the CUDA runtime is used, not cuBLAS or cuSOLVER.\n\n**Choices you may want to revisit**\n- **Timing:** the timed region covers the factorization plus the upper-triangle zeroing, with a device sync. Input generation and the optional `-v` and `-r` work are not timed, matching the original. Because the matrix is device-resident, host-to-device transfers are excluded.\n- **Single GPU:** I used device 0 only. The machine has four RTX 3090s, but multi-GPU would add a lot of complexity, so I did not do it.\n- **Precision:** no fast-math; the arithmetic stays IEEE double.\n\n**Verification**\n- The build is warning-free with `-Wall -Wextra`.\n- `-v` passes at n = 1, 2, 63, 64, 65, 100, 127, 128, 129, 300, 512, 1000, and 2049, with relative errors around 1e-14 to 1e-11. `-n 0` matches the original's behavior.\n- `-r` output for n = 8 matches the original's values to about 1e-16 relative.
